name: fix_flask_response_leak
description: Stops a Flask blueprint leaking password_hash by returning a public projection
prompts: The users blueprint in app/routes/users.py returns the repository dict directly on both POST /users and GET /users/<id>, so every response includes password_hash. Fix the leak across two files: (1) add a helper to app/repository.py (e.g. public_view(user) -> dict) that returns only id and username; (2) use it in both handlers in app/routes/users.py so no response contains password_hash (or any password field). POST still returns 201 with id and username; GET returns 200 with id and username, or 404 for a missing user.

setup_files.app/__init__.py:
from flask import Flask

from app.routes.users import users_bp


def create_app():
    app = Flask(__name__)
    app.register_blueprint(users_bp)
    return app

test_setup_files.test_leak.py:
from app import create_app

client = create_app().test_client()

r = client.post("/users", json={"username": "ada", "password": "s3cret"})
assert r.status_code == 201, r.data
body = r.get_json()
assert "password_hash" not in body and "password" not in body, f"create leaked: {body}"
assert body.get("username") == "ada" and "id" in body, body

r = client.get("/users/1")
assert r.status_code == 200, r.data
assert "password_hash" not in r.get_json(), f"get leaked: {r.get_json()}"

assert client.get("/users/999").status_code == 404
print("PASS")
